newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Oil execs call for more risk management in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Oil execs call for more risk management in Africa.

text.p: Africa's political leaders and economic planners are generally ignorant of the importance of risk management in the drive to fully exploit the continent's expanding business opportunities, oil industry officials said on Wednesday.

"Quite simply we must...go out there and educate people, especially in government, that we cannot do it alone," Taiwo Idemudia, Nigerian National Petroluem Corporation group general manager (crude oil marketing) told an African oil conference in Harare.

"Certainly there is need for an education process but I think people are beginning to understand and investigate the importance of risk management," added Kyle Harris of the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX).

The four-day conference, organised by the Nairobi-based PTA Bank, Zimbabwe's National Oil Company and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development, has brought together African energy and finance officials for an update on the latest oil marketing, risk management and financing techniques.

Idemudia said key problems facing Nigeria's oil industry included the absence of risk management policies, an enabling financial environment, confusing signals on privatisation and ignorance among government officials.
"We must go beyond New York, Houston and London and make politicians understand the need for risk management," he said.
Harris told the conference many governments were increasingly relying on risk management for accurate budgeting given the volatility of oil prices.
